Synopsis:
First dialogue with Hope's spirit that happens after players get to House of Hope.Hope is a captive within the House, and has been driven mad by years of psychological and physical torture. Raphael keeps her alive because she astonishes him - and the reason for that is that no matter what he does to her, she holds onto the last of her hope and optimism. That fascinates him.In this dialogue, Hope introduces players to the House of Hope. They have arrived here deliberately, knowing that they are not invited, and that it is likely dangerous.Hope appears to warn them of that danger, and to help them, and also introduces the deranged vibe of the area.Note: When Hope speaks in all-caps, she is showing the manic side of her personality. Louder, more intense, and almost like she's possessed by a different, more deranged version of herself.

Cluster Contexts:
- LOW_HouseOfHope_HopeSpirit01.json: The player party has deliberately come, uninvited and likely unwelcome, to the House of Hope and this is their first meeting with Hope’s spirit. Hope is a long‑suffering captive of the House — driven mad by years of psychological and physical torture — and kept alive by Raphael because her stubborn optimism fascinates him. She appears as a flickering, sometimes spectral figure who winces from ongoing pain, warns the party that the place is dangerous, and can fade away if frightened or threatened. When her lines appear in ALL‑CAPS she’s lurching into a manic, possession‑like intensity that underlines the deranged tone of the area.
- LOW_HouseOfHope_Hope.json: Off-screen the party has already freed Hope in person (she is not a spirit) and she has begun following the player. The immediate moment comes after the party’s victory over Raphael, so Raphael’s defeat and Hope’s rescue are recent and relevant to the lines. Hope is shaken and euphoric—alternating fear that this is still a dream with exuberant relief—and repeatedly mentions “my beautiful sister,” who fought the party but survived despite being badly hurt. The player can now ask who Hope is, why she was imprisoned, and how she was connected to Raphael; her dialogue reflects trauma, gratitude, and complicated feelings toward her sister and her captors.
- LOW_HouseOfHope_AD_HopeCallsToTalk.json: While players are exploring House of Hope, Hope can appear to tell about the rooms. She will call, so player would paid attention to her
- LOW_HouseOfHope_AD_HopePleads.json: The player is at the threshold of leaving the House of Hope without having freed Hope; as they approach the foyer she suddenly appears to stop them. Off‑screen the party may already have explored rooms or fought occupants of the house, but opted not to or failed to rescue her, prompting this interception. Hope’s lines are panicked and accusatory — she pleads that the player is “her only friend” while also sounding hurt and betrayed (the “how dare you” edge). Companion presence and earlier choices can change tone and exact wording, so these excerpts show two possible emotional variants (frantic begging vs. desperate accusation) rather than the full set of outcomes.
- LOW_DevilsFee_RitualCircle.json: Dialog to invoke the ritual to go to House of Hope from Lower City.RELEVANT NOTE: This dialog will only appear at the first time players go to house of hope. Later, this never will be triggered again.

context: The party has just arrived—uninvited and likely unwelcome—at the House of Hope, and this is their first meeting with Hope’s spirit. Off‑screen she has been a long‑suffering captive kept alive by Raphael, who studies and tortures her because her stubborn optimism fascinates him; years of abuse have left her traumatized and unstable. She appears as a flickering, sometimes spectral figure who winces from pain, speaks in playful rhymes one moment and MANIC, all‑caps warnings the next, and cautions the party that the house is dangerous and that a “jailor” might hear them. Threats, sudden pain, or hostility can make her fade away, though she can also be gently persuaded to return.
